title: Adjacency Matrix: how to decide where to expand after PMF
summary: Jason Cohen gives a framework for choosing expansion moves after product/market fit. Score each idea by how much marketing, sales, service, product, engineering and business model must change (trivial, adjustment, overhaul). Multiple overhauls make an idea a bad bet unless the upside is enormous. He illustrates it with WP Engine's enterprise options.

principles.text: Expand only when growth is bottlenecked, your market is saturating, you want diversification, or you can afford to lose the bet.
principles.quote: If existing marketing and sales channels are at their limit--when spending more time or money doesn't yield more output, or at least, not cost-efficiently. In that case, an expansion to a new channel, or new geography, or new market segment, accelerates growth.

principles.text: A great strategy that doesn't leverage your existing strengths is a bad strategy for you. Judge expansion ideas by adjacency.
principles.quote: A great strategy--that doesn't align with your strengths--is a bad strategy _for you_.

principles.text: Rate each functional area as Trivial, Adjustment, or Overhaul for a new idea. Forcing three buckets avoids false precision.
principles.quote: Now evaluate the "adjacency" of your proposal by determining **how much each of these activities must change** to support the new initiative.

principles.text: More than one area needing a full overhaul is a deal-breaker for incremental innovation, unless you accept big investment, big risk, and enormous upside.
principles.quote: In particular, when more than one area requires a "full overhaul," that's a deal-breaker if this is supposed to be an incremental, sustaining innovation.

principles.text: Early startups claiming an enterprise growth path at ~$500k ARR are usually wrong. Start with simple use-cases at larger companies instead.
principles.quote: Often startups claim this as their growth path, even when they're at only $500k in ARR. This is definitely the wrong strategy at that moment

principles.text: Expanding into a different segment diversifies positioning and makes growth robust to downturns. At WP Engine, small firms saw it as expensive and large firms as low cost.
principles.quote: When one segment has difficulty, the other grows; the net effect is stability.
